by Beretta Holding to purchase more than 2.4M shares of the gunmaker at a price of $44.80 per share.
This represents a premium of ~21% to Wednesday’s closing price.
The tender offer is part of an agreement between Beretta and Sturm, Ruger
that allows the former to increase its stake in Sturm, Ruger
from 10% to 25%. In exchange for an increased stake, Beretta would drop its proxy fight for control of its U.S. rival.

The agreement also allows Beretta the right to nominate up to two independent directors and imposes a standstill period of three years during which Beretta cannot attempt a takeover or proxy fight for Sturm, Ruger

The consent agreement between the two settles allegations that Beretta and Ruger’s proposed stock deal would create an "illegal interlocking" directorate arrangement in violation of Section 8 of the Clayton Act, prohibiting directors and officers from serving simultaneously on the boards of competitors.

title: Beretta launches cash tender offer for Sturm, Ruger shares
